articles.title: Bank Of Japan Holds Key Rate As Expected
articles.expand: The Bank of Japan left its key interest rate unchanged on Friday after a hike last month as underlying inflation is assessed to be consistent with the 2 percent inflation target. The policy board, governed by Ueda Kazu, voted 8-1 in favor of holding the interest rate at 1.25 percent, the highest since 1995.

articles.title: BOJ declares inflation victory but still won't budge on rates, so what's the hold-up?
articles.expand: If you think back to a decade ago, the BOJ being able to even see the path to reach the inflation target was very much a pipedream. Yet, here we are today. The central bank finally gets to declare victory on inflation. That must mean champagne all around, surely? Well, not quite. As it would seem, getting to the finish line and convincing policymakers to do something about it are two very different things. The BOJ kept its policy rate unchanged today at 1.25% in a 8-1 vote, with board member Takata dissenting in playing the role as the lone hawk again. He called for a 25 bps rate hike to 1.50%...
